summary: Run this rewrite stage only after s5-copy-safe-forced has been harvested and its judged profile actually contains wgmma rows with a mixed per-cell outcome. Before the s5 data exists it has nothing to stand on, and the prepare-time evidence so far makes a mixed outcome unlikely: both kernels beat Marlin by about the same margin.
justification: The mechanism is plausible. In the judged profiles, Marlin's two calls take 306.2 us at bs=128 and 483.2 us at bs=256 (s4, job 4e7f8be895a145ba). The floors are 101.3 and 108.9 us, so there is 3-4.5x of headroom on 2 of the 6 equally weighted loads. A per-cell enable that keeps only the winning kernel is a sound way to stage the rewrite. The expected directions (bs=128/256 faster, bs=16 flat) fit TASK.md: T<128 runs master. The weakest link is that the s6 decision table has no data behind it yet. No judged profile has ever contained a wgmma row: s1 failed to build, s2 fell back, s3 failed, and in s4 the copy-unsafe gate silently ran Marlin. The only per-kernel evidence is s4's prepare timing. At M=128 cold that was w13+silu 385.6 vs Marlin w13+act 611.6 (0.63x) and w2 185.4 vs 310.0 (0.60x); at M=256 it was 457.2 vs 852.0 (0.54x) and 230.2 vs 425.9 (0.54x). Both kernels win by nearly the same ratio, so the most likely s5 outcome is all cells win (s6 is skipped in favour of the s5 gated twin) or all cells lose (the line closes). Only the mixed case gives s6 something to do. Second weakness: the prepare timings ran an all-local routing (1024 local routes at M=128). There Marlin reads ~920 us against 306 us judged, so the routing does not look like the judge's. The LESSONS-173 selector must use the judge-like skewed routing, where per-expert M is much smaller and the two kernels' ratio may differ. Third: path (b) needs a new wgmma epilogue that scatters h into Marlin's cache2 route-row layout, and that code has never run. Path (c), Marlin cache2 into wgmma w2, has been self-checked at rel 3.5e-3. Finally, a single profile's 0.95x threshold sits inside the about ±20% run-to-run noise of a Marlin row (REWRITE_READ). The static table should only nominate cells, and the selector's ≥1.02x graph-replay confirmation should decide.
confounders: marlin-block-m-two-smaller-on-postnorm: sets master's block_size_m at T>=128 (16 at M=128, 32 at M=256 per the s4 log). It defines the incumbent Marlin cells that paths (b), (c) and (d) compare against, and it decides whether wgmma can share the Marlin align (16-row m-blocks) at B256. If it were reverted, the incumbent would be slower and the per-cell table would shift towards wgmma. That is not a confound of the s6 result, but the table is only valid for this block_size_m.

align-parallel-per-expert-verify: master's T>32 align. Mixed paths (b) and (c) need it plus possibly a second align for wgmma at B256 (~4-7 us). That cost lands on the mixed cells and not on (a) or (d), so a mixed cell's gain must clear it.
w2-marlin-atomic-add-small-m: T<=32 only, so it is disjoint from the 128<=T<=512 cells. No confound beyond the rebase that s4 already did.

post-expert-norm-triton-small-m / SGLang fused_post_expert_norm at bs>=32: every path feeds the same combine. Path (a)'s wgmma w2 output layout ('fused norm skips remote rows') differs from Marlin's, so check that the combine input layout is identical across (a), (b), (c) and (d), or the combine time becomes a hidden per-path variable.
interference: No companion. This is kind: rewrite, judged per cell on the replaced kernels' own profile rows (wgmma w13+silu vs Marlin call 1 + act_and_mul; wgmma w2 vs Marlin call 2) within the same run. That attribution is internal, and no reverted or retuned landed hypothesis would sharpen it. The landed changes that touch this range (block_size_m pick, T>32 align) define the incumbent and are not alternative explanations for a per-kernel row delta. With 5 moe checks left and s5-forced still unrun, a companion would spend a check that s5 needs. The real control is the dispatch gate in the hypothesis's own Risk section: run s6 only if s5's judged rows split. If s5 shows all-win or all-lose, do not run s6.
rules_flags: Path choice must use T plus prepare booleans only, and the static table must be literals from the s5 profile. The prepare selector must time synthetic judge-like routings, never anything from data. As specified this complies; keep it that way.

Path (b)'s new cache2-layout epilogue must write every route row Marlin w2 will read, and leave remote/padded rows unread rather than read stale. Stale cache2 rows from a previous replay would reproduce s3's cross-copy failure mode. Include path (b) in the three-state (A, deepcopy B, clone C) refill-replay check with mixed local and remote routing.
Per-call cuTensorMapEncode on the host at capture time (inherited from s5) is fine. No module-level caching of maps or pointers is allowed. Re-run s4's global audit on the s6 source.

Budget: s4 already hit a 235 s replay deadline guard. Adding a 41-rep selector per enabled cell (up to 4) and a three-state check per enabled mix risks the 300 s prepare limit and the 15-minute run limit. Keep the cheap fallback: any check skipped for budget means that cell runs (d).
open_questions: Did s5-forced log LAUNCHED = wgmma and produce judged wgmma kernel rows at bs=128 and 256? If not, s6 has no table and should not run.

Did the per-cell judged ratios actually split across the 0.95x line? The prepare ratios (0.54-0.63 for both kernels) predict they will not. If they do not, this slug should close as superseded by the s5 gated twin or the line closure.

At B256, does the wgmma kernel get its own 16-row align (an extra ~5-7 us launch) or reuse Marlin's 32-row align? The spec leaves this open. The cost of a second align must be inside the selector's timed graph so the ≥1.02x test sees it.

Is the prepare selector's 'judge-like routing' the skewed, this-GPU-busiest distribution (per-expert M far below all-local)? s4's prepare timings used 1024 local routes at M=128 and overstated Marlin by about 3x against the judge.
How are the bs=257 and skewed bs=128 tests bucketed (B256 cell vs B128 cell)? Each must hit an enabled mix that the three-state check has verified.
